propositions: Negative caplog assertions (assert not [...]) pass vacuously when zero records are captured, failing to detect lost coverage silently while the test reports green.

Logger propagation disabled globally via logging.getLogger('rebar').propagate=False and logger level raised via setLevel(WARNING) are never restored, poisoning downstream tests' log capture in nondeterministic order.

Five specific negative-assertion tests are targets of void-coverage risk; instrumentation confirmed all five reach their assertions with propagate=True and all five fail when forbidden records are injected, so zero are currently void but the class defect remains.

An autouse pytest fixture in tests/_log_integrity.py guards against propagation=False at test setup (failing at source and restoring) and contains logger-level mutations at teardown, converting silent fail-open into loud fail-closed.

The guard does not duplicate b718's production-code fix (configure_logging no longer sets propagate=False); instead it catches the logger-level poisoning vector and any future propagation changes, and makes ordering non-determinism irrelevant to coverage integrity.
